engagement_title: Cedarline Institute autumn cohort: decide which of two dead press files can still carry a run, recover a seal that survives only as an impression, and deliver a whole cohort at two registers plus a programme and a credential card the office can edit
vertical: Continuing professional education, independent institute running a community evening programme and an employer funded executive programme from two campus buildings (Vermont)
real_brief_anchor: The batch record carried no quoted posting for this entry, so the anchor is reconstructed from the recurring certificate merge brief that runs constantly on Upwork and Freelancer.com: a training provider with a roster spreadsheet and a certificate design nobody can edit any more, asking for every candidate's certificate personalised and print ready, one file per person for emailing, and the institution's seal and signatures reproduced exactly. Laundered to the fictional Cedarline Institute (registrar Helen Abbott, signatories Dr Miriam Voss and Callum Reyes); no real school, awarding body, person or trademark is named. The ledger's verdict was REBUILD because the entry as first carved was a single merge and nothing else. The commission a provider of this shape actually posts is bigger in three specific ways it always states out loud: the cohort is not one register but two at very different price points, the artwork is gone and survives only as a physical impression, and the ceremony needs a programme and a shareable credential the office can correct up to the morning.
client_one_liner: The autumn cohort finishes in five weeks, our print shop closed with the seal die, and two thirds of the cohort paid a hundred and eighty dollars while the rest are on a nine thousand dollar employer funded programme.
client_brief:
Cedarline Institute, autumn cohort credentials

We run continuing professional education out of two buildings in Vermont. The autumn cohort finishes in five weeks. Every candidate has to leave the ceremony with a certificate in hand and a file in their inbox the same evening.

The cohort is not one thing. About two thirds are on the community programme, a hundred and eighty dollar evening course, and that certificate is a plain honest thing that goes on a kitchen wall. The rest are on the executive programme, which costs nine thousand dollars and is bought by employers, and that credential ends up framed in an office where clients see it. Those two cannot come off the press looking identical. If the executive diploma reads like a printable freebie we will hear about it from the sponsoring firms inside a week.

The shop that printed for us closed. We have two files: last year's community certificate, and the executive diploma we have not changed since twenty nineteen. Use whichever of them still works.

We need the whole cohort as one file for the printer, a separate file for each candidate named to them so the office can send them out individually, and a full quality proof of one of each kind for me to sign before anything is printed.

The seal is the problem. The die went with the closed shop. All we have is a certificate with the seal pressed into it and a photograph of that impression. We need it back as artwork we can use anywhere, and it has to be the same seal on the printed credential and on anything digital.

We also need the ceremony programme with the full cohort listed, and something graduates can post afterwards. Both have to be editable here, because names get corrected right up to the morning.

Please flag anything in the registrar's export that looks wrong rather than printing it.
price_band_and_audience: Two credentials, one cohort, an order of magnitude apart. The community certificate at 180 dollars is earned by evening students in their twenties and thirties and is read by family: plain, warm, legible, honest about what it is. The executive credential at 9,000 dollars is bought by employers and read by that graduate's own clients on an office wall: heavier engraved register, generous margins, restrained colour, the seal given room. The band is load bearing in both directions. Give the community certificate the executive treatment and it becomes pompous about an evening course, which embarrasses the student. Give the executive credential the community treatment and a sponsoring firm sees a printable freebie in a frame, which is the specific failure the registrar says she will hear about within a week. A cohort run of this shape posts at 600 to 1,500 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Independent continuing professional education institute running a community evening programme and an employer funded executive programme from two campus buildings.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 1978, two campus buildings in Vermont, cohort run by registrar Helen Abbott.
brand_identity.about: Cedarline teaches working adults across two very different registers: an accessible community evening course and a high cost executive programme bought by employers. Each autumn cohort finishes with a ceremony where every candidate leaves with a certificate in hand and a file in their inbox the same evening. The Institute trades on being trusted rather than flashy, and on the two credentials reading honestly for what they cost.
brand_identity.audience: Community students in their twenties and thirties whose certificate is read by family at home, and executive candidates whose employer funded credential ends up framed in an office where their own clients see it.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Two credentials an order of magnitude apart: a 180 dollar community certificate and a 9,000 dollar employer funded executive credential. Neither can come off the press looking like the other. Cohort run posts around 600 to 1,500 dollars fixed.
brand_identity.typography: An engraved, higher contrast serif for the executive register, set with generous margins and the seal given room. A warmer, plainly legible serif for the community certificate. The two share bones but never the same weight or spacing.
brand_identity.voice: Measured and earned, never boastful. We state what was completed and who signed it. Example line the brand would write: 'Completed the autumn programme in professional practice. Signed at Cedarline Institute, Vermont.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The seal die went to the printer that closed and cannot be recovered. The only surviving seal is the one blind embossed into an old certificate, plus a raking light photograph of that impression. Two dead press files remain, last year's community certificate and the 2019 executive diploma; there is no digital seal artwork.
brand_identity.values: Each credential must be honest about its price, and every candidate name spelled and accented correctly right up to the ceremony morning.

assets_supplied.name: adulted_2024_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: Last year's community completion certificate as a flat press PDF, A4 landscape, fonts embedded, produced from a real page layout so it converts cleanly. Carries a recipient name, a programme title, a completion date, a small letterspaced credential number, two signature lines and a seal position.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Last year's community certificate. It is what the shop printed from."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The conversion exposes the recipient name, the programme title, the completion date and the credential number inside ONE continuous flow while the two signatory lines sit alone, and the mapping readout omits the letterspaced credential number run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed and every offset past it is short by that run's length. The validator returns VALID on those offsets, the prepare call reports success, and the fields past the omission are silently absent from the template.

assets_supplied.name: exec_diploma_2019_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The executive diploma as a flat press PDF, produced in 2019 by a different print shop from the community certificate and unchanged since.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The executive diploma. We have not touched it since twenty nineteen."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: How this document was built is nothing like how the printed page reads. Its whole face is one continuous typeset block, so the conversion yields a single text frame holding every line and no graphic frame at all, which means there is no target to bind a per record seal into and every field has to be driven by offset arithmetic inside one story. Nothing about the printed diploma suggests this, and it is not visible until the document has actually been converted and its interchange file read.

assets_supplied.name: cohort_export.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The registrar's export for the autumn cohort, one row per candidate, with columns for name, programme code, programme title, completion date, credential number and an honours field.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The full cohort straight out of the student system."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Four faults, none stated. Which register a candidate belongs to is carried only inside the programme code, so the two tiers have to be inferred rather than filtered. One candidate withdrew in week three and was never removed. Two rows carry the same credential number, a clerical duplicate that would put an identical number on two different people's credentials. And several names carry European diacritics typed in a convention the rest of the file does not use, while the honours column is empty for the entire community register even though the certificate face carries an honours line.

assets_supplied.name: seal_impression.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: A raking light photograph of the institutional seal blind embossed into cream certificate stock: a rope bordered ring enclosing a cedar device and the institute's founding year.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The die went with the shop. This is the only seal we have left, pressed into an old certificate."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The impression is colourless: relief and paper are the same cream, and the seal reads only as shadow. Where the raking light falls away along one side of the ring the relief and the stock sit at the same luminance, so a selection there has nothing to hold on to. The mask still comes back looking like a seal, the trace still succeeds, and what is missing is an arc of the rope border and part of the year, which is invisible against cream at preview scale.

assets_supplied.name: campus_frames/ (6 staff photographs)
assets_supplied.kind: Six photographs of the ceremony hall and the two campus buildings, shot on staff phones across two afternoons for the programme cover and the credential card.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our own pictures of the hall and the buildings."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three were shot with the phone's high dynamic range mode on and carry a milky lifted black point that looks perfectly clean alone and turns visibly grey the moment it sits next to one of the other three. One hall interior sits a degree off level, and straightening it consumes exactly the edge margin the programme cover's crop wants.

assets_supplied.name: registrar_note.txt
assets_supplied.kind: A page from Helen Abbott on how the two programmes are described, who signs which credential, and what the sponsoring firms have complained about before.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "How we talk about the two programmes and who signs what."

acceptance_bar: Exactly one credential per candidate who genuinely completed, no extra and no missing, and any row not printed is named to the registrar with the reason.
The two registers are visibly different credentials at a glance, in type register, in margin and in how the seal is given room, and both are unmistakably from the same institute.
No two candidates carry the same credential number, and every name is set the way that candidate spells it, diacritics included.
Every field the printed face carries is present on every credential and nothing ends mid line at trim.
The seal is recovered whole: the rope border closes all the way round and the founding year is complete, judged on the cream ground at print resolution rather than on screen.
The seal on the printed credential and the seal on anything digital are the same artwork, not two versions of it.
Each per candidate file contains the candidate its filename claims, established by opening it rather than by the order the files came back.
Both proofs are rendered at true print resolution at credential trim, not at screen scale.
The six campus photographs read as one set, with one black point, and any frame that cannot join is named rather than shipped.
No delivered image exceeds its source dimensions and no crop tradeoff record carries an upscale entry.

The ceremony programme and the credential card come back as a native editable document the office can correct a name in on the morning, with every photograph actually visible, the cohort roster as a real table with every candidate present and legible, and every text element carrying its licensed face at that family's own weight.

A written note: which press file was used for which register and why the other was handled differently, every export row questioned and how it was resolved, what was applied to each photograph, the type system by role, and every resize any tool reported.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd (twice), export_idml (repeatedly), generate_indd_mapping_prompt (as generator and as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (application/x-indesign and application/pdf, additionalImageFiles, recordRange), document_render_layout (resolution 300, createSeparateFiles, pageRange in N-N form)
adobe_surfaces.role: The credential run and the headline deliverable, carried out twice because the cohort is two registers. Two dead press files are converted and inspected, the survivable route for each register is decided from what the conversions actually expose, the reconciled roster becomes a data source, and the run produces the printer's file, the per candidate files the office emails, and the two proofs the registrar signs. True story text is rebuilt from the exported interchange file rather than trusted from the convenience readout, and placeholder inventories are confirmed by round trip rather than by a success message.

adobe_surfaces.tools: asset upload and asset_inline_preview, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_invert_selection, image_crop_to_bounds, image_vectorize, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments, image_apply_auto_tone, image_crop_and_resize (reading tradeoffs and detection_confidence)
adobe_surfaces.role: The seal recovery and the campus set. The seal exists only as a colourless impression photographed in raking light, so it has to be selected as relief rather than as an object, inverted, cropped to its own bbox and traced, then have its opaque background path stripped and a viewBox injected before it is placeable anywhere. The same surface levels the off level hall frame, pulls the three high dynamic range frames back to the black point the other three hold, and derives the programme and card crops at native scale while reading the tradeoff record on every call.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The ceremony programme and the graduate credential card as one native editable document with mixed canvases in a single export: the programme spread carrying the full cohort roster as a genuine table, and a square card and a wide banner a graduate can post. The recovered seal is inlined as SVG so it arrives as editable vector rather than a picture, every photograph is carried as embedded image data because a photograph left as a URL renders as an empty grey box, and each root declares its own canvas so a global override cannot collapse the set.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system for the programme and the credential card, and the only place the agent's typographic authorship exists, since neither merged credential can receive a font from this surface: those pages inherit whatever the two closed print shops embedded. The pairing has to carry an evening course and an employer funded credential in one institutional voice, the numeric weight cannot be inferred from a style name, one unlaundered name falls back silently to a default sans, and the CSS must use the returned slug.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one establishing frame the programme cover needs and the institute does not own, IP clean, at camera scale, with generative candidates excluded, because the alternative is putting an unlicensed photograph on a document handed to every family at a ceremony. The Boards half persists the registrar's sign off set, the two proofs and the recovered seal, before a cohort's worth of printing is committed, placed within the twelve per call cap with a 201 read as partial success.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable goes to which surface.
trajectory.judgement: The credentials are record per page against faces the institute wants kept, so they belong to the merge surface; the programme and the card must stay correctable on the morning of the ceremony, which the merge surface structurally cannot give.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming a surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload both press files, the cohort export, the seal photograph, the six campus frames and the registrar's note, holding every returned presigned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A manifest keyed by register and by role, because the run forks in two and the same artwork will exist in several states.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by register and role.

trajectory.action: Read the export against the registrar's note and reconcile it: split the cohort into its two registers off the programme code, resolve the withdrawal, the duplicate credential number, the diacritic convention and the empty honours column.
trajectory.judgement: None of this is filtering. Which faults the agent may fix and which belong to the registrar's own record system is a judgement, and the client asked to be told rather than printed around.
trajectory.produces: Two normalised register files and a written list of questions for the registrar.

trajectory.action: Preview the seal photograph closely and plan the recovery: what the impression actually gives a selection to hold, and which element of the device to name.
trajectory.judgement: A blind embossed seal is not an object with an edge, it is a relief read as shadow, and naming the certificate or the paper pulls the selection to the substrate instead of the device.
trajectory.produces: A recovery plan naming the element to select and the fallback if it will not hold.

trajectory.action: Select the seal's relief, invert, crop to the returned bbox and trace, then strip the opaque background path and inject a viewBox.
trajectory.judgement: Polarity before tracing decides whether the result is a mark or a black box, and the trace accepts no options at all, so every lever lives in the raster preparation.
trajectory.produces: A first transparent, scalable SVG of the institutional seal.

trajectory.action: Lay the traced seal at credential size on the cream ground the stock has and read the device round the whole ring rather than glancing at it.
trajectory.judgement: The only place a recovered mark can be judged is at reproduction size on the real ground, and the whole point of a seal is that it closes.
trajectory.produces: An inspected seal at reproduction size, in or out, with the reasoning recorded.

trajectory.action: Convert BOTH press files, export the interchange file for each, unzip them and read the real frame inventories, bounds and object styles.
trajectory.judgement: The printed face says nothing about how a document was built, and the two files came from two different shops, so neither can be assumed to behave like the other.
trajectory.produces: Two converted documents, two interchange exports and a frame inventory for each with real integer ids and bounds.

trajectory.action: Rebuild each frame's true story text by concatenating its content runs, and compute every offset from that string.
trajectory.judgement: The convenience readout is not the document. Offsets taken from it are short past any run it omits, and nothing downstream complains.
trajectory.produces: A reconstructed story string per frame and an offset table computed from it.

trajectory.action: Decide the architecture for each register against what the two conversions actually exposed, and record why.
trajectory.judgement: This is the engagement's structural decision and it cannot be made before the documents have been opened. What each file can carry, and what a register loses if it is moved to the other file, is the whole question.
trajectory.produces: A stated route per register with the tradeoff each one costs.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping for each route, validate it, prepare each template, then export the interchange file from each RESULT and search it for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: A success message is not evidence, and rows sharing one frame must be ordered so their positions hold against the original text.
trajectory.produces: Prepared templates whose placeholder inventories have been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge each register to a native document, binding the seal per record where a graphic frame exists to receive it.
trajectory.judgement: Merging to the native document first keeps both the press branch and the per candidate branch open off one merge.
trajectory.produces: A merged native document per register.

trajectory.action: Render one proof from each register at true print resolution at credential trim and read the whole face, seal included.
trajectory.judgement: The rendered page at trim is the only place the seal's recovery and the template's own behaviour are both visible at once.

trajectory.action: Render both registers in full at trim and read every page against the reconciled roster, name by name and number by number.
trajectory.judgement: A missing field and a duplicated credential number both look like success at the API boundary and both look acceptable on a screen scale proxy.
trajectory.produces: A page by page reconciliation against both register files.

trajectory.action: Produce the per candidate single page files from the merged documents and name each by opening it.
trajectory.judgement: Identity by position in a returned list is the fast wrong answer that emails one graduate another graduate's credential.
trajectory.produces: One named single credential file per candidate, verified by inspection.

trajectory.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, and Adobe Stock
trajectory.action: Level the off level hall frame, bring the six campus photographs to one black point, derive the programme and card crops reading tradeoffs on every call, and license one establishing frame the institute does not own.
trajectory.judgement: Three frames look clean alone and grey beside the other three, and straightening the hall eats the edge the cover crop wants, so the order matters. Short generic queries only, and the orientation filter always returns zero.
trajectory.produces: A graded campus set with tradeoff records and one licensed camera scale frame.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own and has to hold an evening course and an employer funded credential in one institutional voice. Weight cannot be inferred from a style name.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual numeric weight per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the programme spread with the full cohort roster as a real table, plus the square credential card and the wide banner, each root declaring its own canvas, every photograph inlined as image data, the recovered seal inlined as SVG, family and weight declared per element; upload it and hold the URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set. How a cohort of that size is set as a roster is a real typographic decision.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML retained as the durable source.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify canvas one from the document's rendition and every other canvas from the returned per canvas markup, roster row by roster row.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition shows the first artboard only, so the markup is the only channel for anything past it.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document, an inspected first canvas and a markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Build the registrar's sign off board within the placement cap, re sending only entries named as failed, then write the note.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success. The note has to name every export row questioned and every route decision, because the registrar asked to be flagged rather than printed around.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether this photograph of a blind embossed seal will give up the whole device. The impression is colourless, so relief and paper are the same cream and the seal exists only as shadow. Along the side where the raking light falls away the relief and the stock sit at the same luminance and the selection has nothing to hold, so the mask silently loses an arc of the rope border and part of the founding year. Nothing reports it: the selection succeeds, the mask thumbnail still looks like a seal, the trace succeeds, and the gap is invisible against cream at preview scale. It becomes visible only with the traced seal placed at credential size on the cream ground.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it and care cannot prevent it: the failure is a property of where the light fell on this one photograph, and there is no measurement anywhere in the family, no histogram and no eyedropper, so no read ahead exists. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says only that the die is gone and the seal must come back as usable artwork; no asset note or acceptance line discloses that part of it will not select. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a different instrument, either compositing per element selections or abandoning the impression for the flat printed seal on the old certificate face.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Confirm the loss by reading the traced seal round the whole ring at reproduction size rather than glancing at the thumbnail, then re attack it: name the rope border and the year as their own selections and composite them with the ring, or crop far tighter so the shadowed side carries more pixels, or fall back to the seal printed on the 2024 certificate face and accept that it is a different generation of the same device, which is a provenance decision the registrar has to be told about.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Every credential in the cohort, community and executive alike, carries an institutional seal with a broken rope border and half a founding year, on a document that hangs on a wall for twenty years and whose whole function is to look unforgeable.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What each of the two press files can actually carry. The community certificate converts into a usable structure with a graphic frame that can receive a per record seal. The 2019 executive diploma, built by a different shop as one continuous typeset block, converts into a SINGLE text frame holding every line and NO graphic frame at all, so there is no target to bind a seal into and all four fields must be driven by offset arithmetic inside one story. Nothing about the printed diploma suggests this: it looks like the more carefully made of the two documents. Frame granularity from a PDF is not under anyone's control and is exposed only by converting and reading the interchange file.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it. Converting both and looking IS the correct move, and what it returns is not knowable in advance from the printed pages, the file sizes or anything the client said. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says only that there are two files and to use whichever still works, which is the client's ignorance, not a disclosure of which one fails or how. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is an architecture decision that changes what the executive register can be, how its seal is placed, and what the agent has to tell the registrar.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re plan the executive register around what its file can hold: drive its fields by offsets inside the one story, decide whether its seal can be placed at all through the merge or whether that register has to ride the community derived template at a corrected type register, weigh what a 9,000 dollar credential loses either way against the registrar's stated fear of looking like a printable freebie, then rebuild the mapping and re verify the placeholders for that register from scratch.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The executive register either merges with no seal at all, or is quietly run off the community template, and the employer funded credential arrives at the ceremony looking exactly like the 180 dollar evening certificate in front of the sponsoring firms the registrar named.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the importer does with the cohort roster once the table is taller than the artboard it sits on. A table survives as a live table, but nothing anywhere documents what happens past the canvas edge: whether rows are clipped, reflowed, hoisted or dropped. The export returns success either way with no warning of any kind, and because the roster sits on a canvas after the first, the rendition cannot show it, so the returned per canvas markup is the only channel through which the roster's actual state exists. Counting rows in the markup is the only way to learn whether the whole cohort is in the programme.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it and care cannot settle it, because how many rows the artboard holds at a chosen size and leading is not computable from anything the connector exposes, and the check itself only exists after an export. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for the programme with the full cohort listed and for it to be editable; no asset note, deliverable or earlier step says anything about roster length or canvas behaviour. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is an authoring decision about how a cohort is broken across pages and set in two registers.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Count the roster rows present in the returned markup against the reconciled register files rather than trusting slide_count, and where rows are missing, re author the programme: split the roster across additional canvases, decide where the two registers break and whether they are listed together or apart, re set the measure and leading so the names with diacritics still fit their cells, then re run the readiness check and export again and re count.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The ceremony programme handed to every family in the hall silently omits the last dozen graduates, whose relatives are sitting there, and the office finds out during the ceremony rather than before it.

deliverables.name: Autumn cohort credential run: printer's file, per candidate files and two signed proofs
deliverables.spec: One credential per completing candidate across two registers, page count equal to the reconciled roster, each binding name, programme title, completion date, credential number and honours verbatim with the institutional seal in place. Delivered as the printer's multi page file, as one named single page file per candidate verified by opening it, and as one 300 DPI proof per register at credential trim for the registrar's signature. Produced by reverse engineering two closed print shops' press files into whatever live route each can actually carry, with the templates and the reasoning handed back.

deliverables.name: Recovered Cedarline institutional seal
deliverables.spec: The institute's seal recovered from a colourless embossed impression as a placeable SVG: selected as relief rather than as an object, composited from per element selections where one pass will not hold, traced, with the opaque full canvas background path removed and a viewBox injected so it scales, delivered proven whole (rope border closed, founding year complete) at credential size on cream. Handed back as the institute's only surviving artwork, identical on print and on screen, with the reproduction floor below which it should not be used.

deliverables.name: Ceremony programme and graduate credential card as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: A single native editable document carrying the ceremony programme spread, a square credential card and a wide banner in one export, each keeping its own canvas size, with the full cohort roster as a genuine table with every candidate present and legible, the recovered seal as editable vector, live editable text in one licensed type system, and every photograph carried as embedded image data. Delivered with the self contained source, so the office can correct a name on the morning.

deliverables.name: Campus set for the programme and card
deliverables.spec: Six staff photographs of the hall and the two buildings brought to one declared black point so they read as one set rather than as two afternoons, levelled where needed before any crop, cropped for the canvases that receive them, plus one licensed camera scale establishing frame graded into the same set. Every output at or below its source dimensions with the tradeoff record captured per call, and any frame that cannot join named rather than shipped.

deliverables.name: Handover note and registrar's sign off board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording which press file carried which register and what the other one could not do, every export row questioned (the withdrawal, the duplicate credential number, the diacritic convention, the empty honours column) and how each was resolved, how the seal was recovered and where its provenance changed, the type system by role with family, foundry and actual numeric weight, what was applied to each photograph, and every resize any tool reported. Paired with a persistent shareable board carrying both proofs, the recovered seal and the campus selects for sign off before a cohort's worth of printing commits.
